text:
Mira: Quick question — updating the Node SDK docs for streaming cancel behavior. Do we standardize on client AbortController -> immediate local stream close + send cancel signal to server (so server stops generation ASAP), or do we prefer graceful drain (server finishes buffered tokens)? Also how should Go context cancellation map to HTTP/2 streaming? Example: client aborts but model-run continues on server — what's expected?

Alex: Prefer server stop ASAP on cancel. Client AbortController should: 1) stop delivering tokens to app, 2) send connection close/CANCEL to server (HTTP/2 RST_STREAM or a cancelation proto). Server should stop generation and return a short error/close. For hosted API, treat as non-retryable. For Dedicated, we may continue some cleanup but not keep CPU generating.

Sam: For SDKs: Node should surface an "AbortError" or 'ABORT_ERR' that is distinct from network errors. Go should return context.Canceled. Rust -> Err(Aborted) / Cancelled. Python -> asyncio.CancelledError. This helps app logic decide not to retry.

Mira: Can we get concrete code snippets to paste in docs?

Alex: Node example:
```
const ac = new AbortController();
const res = await fetch('/v1/stream', { signal: ac.signal });
// later
ac.abort(); // stops stream locally and signals server
```
Go example:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) { /* client aborted */ }
```

Kyle: Edge-case: retries. If user aborts, SDK must not auto-retry the same request. Mark as non-retryable and surface that to retry layer. Also suggest adding optional idempotency_key header for server-side safe retries when client didn't abort.

Jen: E2E test note: we'll add tests that simulate AbortController during stream and assert model stops within 200ms and connection returns 499/aborted metric. Also ensure telemetry emits cancellation_reason:client_abort.

Sam: Quick clarification: what status code should server return when client cancels? We use 499 in nginx-land. For our internal API we can send 499 or a protobuf cancel frame. Docs should say 'client-aborted' metric and map to HTTP 499 if proxied.

Mira: I'll add a short section in SDK docs: "Cancel semantics" showing per-language mappings and recommendation to not retry. Will PR to docs repo after this thread. @Kyle can you add the idempotency header suggestion to client retry guide? :thumbsup:

Kyle: On it, will open PR now.

deploy-bot: node-sdk@1.4.2 deployed to staging — includes better AbortError propagation.

Mira: Great — thanks everyone. I'll draft the PR and ping for review. (Adding a small example for streaming clients.)
